title: Kernel closure for finite-discrete constructible internal modules
statement: Let B be a finite commutative ring with its discrete topology and let T be any scheme. Put R=p_T* of the condensed continuous-function ring B [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For internal R-modules M and N constructible by finite scheme stratifications and local finite presentations [def-sfb-constructible-module], the categorical kernel of every R-linear f:M→N is constructible in the same sense. No noetherian assumption on T is needed.

source.place: Section 5.1 and Lemma 5.4.1; constructible Serre theorem in the source library ConstructibleSheaf/KernelCokernel.lean; finite-presentation transport from FiniteDiscreteConstructibleModel.lean

proof.text: Choose the constant-ring isomorphism $e$ and the additive-group-compatible equivalence $G$ using the two existence lemmas, and form the single encoding $E_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-common-finite-discrete-encoding]. Put $H=E_T\nu_T^*$. The module comparison is exact and fully faithful by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]; composing with an equivalence retains these properties. In particular $H$ preserves kernels. For $E_T$, this follows directly from the kernel universal property by applying its inverse equivalence to a test arrow and using the unit and counit. All coefficients here are the same finite ring $\operatorname{ULift}B$, with the ring object transported along $e$.

source.place: Tags 099T (lemma-fully-faithful) and 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible), finite coefficient specialization; internal encoding assembly written by Q60.

proof.text: Apply constructible encoding and then fixed-module constructible origin to $M,N$. Obtain constructible etale module sheaves $F_1,F_2$ and isomorphisms $i_1:H(F_1)\cong M$, $i_2:H(F_2)\cong N$, using the counit of $E_T$. Full faithfulness gives a unique $g:F_1\to F_2$ with $H(g)=i_2^{-1}fi_1$ [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Thus $i_2H(g)=fi_1$. Both origin applications allow an arbitrary scheme and the finite coefficient ring used here.

source.place: Tags 099T (lemma-fully-faithful) and 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible), finite coefficient specialization; internal encoding assembly written by Q60.

proof.text: Set $K=\ker g$. The finite-ring constructible Serre theorem makes $K$ constructible on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, with no Noetherian assumption on $T$. Exactness of comparison and the equivalence $E_T$ give $H(K)\cong\ker H(g)$. The commuting square from Step 2 then gives $H(K)\cong\ker f$: send its kernel inclusion through $i_1$; an arrow annihilated by $f$ factors uniquely after applying $i_1^{-1}$. The resulting inverse maps agree by uniqueness of kernel factorization.

It remains to check internal constructibility of $H(K)=E_T(L)$, $L=\nu_T^*K$. The reverse implication of fixed-module constructible origin makes $L$ intrinsically constructible: there are a finite global stratification $(j_a:S_a\to T)_a$ and, for each $a$, a pro-etale cover $\{u:U\to S_a\}$ with $u^*j_a^*L\cong\underline P_U$ for finite $\operatorname{ULift}B$-modules $P$. The restriction is iterated, first to the stratum and then to the cover member, as in [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Fix $a$ and write $j=j_a$, $S=S_a$. Restriction encoding for $j$ and the $R_T$-module $E_T(L)$, with the unit $E_T^{-1}E_T(L)\cong L$, gives $E_S^{-1}(N_S)\cong j^*L$, where $N_S$ is $\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*)(E_TL)$ with scalars restricted along the coefficient isomorphism $\beta$ between $j^*R_T$ and $R_S$. Restriction encoding again, for $u$ and the $R_S$-module $N_S$, gives $E_U^{-1}(N_U)\cong u^*E_S^{-1}(N_S)\cong u^*j^*L\cong\underline P_U$, where $N_U$ is $\operatorname{mapMod}(u^*)(N_S)$ with scalars restricted along the isomorphism between $u^*R_S$ and $R_U$. Applying $E_U$ and its counit, $N_U\cong E_U(\underline P_U)$, which is finitely presented over $R_U$ by the new encoded-constant lemma. Restriction of scalars along a ring isomorphism $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of module categories; it carries the regular module to one isomorphic to the regular module via $\alpha$, and it preserves finite biproducts and cokernels, so it preserves and reflects finite presentation. Moreover $\operatorname{mapMod}(u^*)$ turns restriction along $\beta$ into restriction along $u^*\beta$, since the transported action is $u^*(\gamma)\circ\mu$ and $\mu$ is natural. Hence $\operatorname{mapMod}(u^*)\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*)(H(K))$ is finitely presented over $u^*j^*R_T$ for every member of every cover. So each $\operatorname{mapMod}(j_a^*)(H(K))$ is locally finitely presented, and $H(K)$ is constructible by [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Finally every $\operatorname{mapMod}$ carries the isomorphism $H(K)\cong\ker f$ to a module isomorphism; composing it with these presentations shows that $\ker f$ is constructible.

from.place: Triangulatedness via constructible heart closure, specifically closure under kernels for finite discrete coefficients; the local finite-presentation transport supplies the finite-coefficient case.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteDiscrete_constructible_kernel
    (B : Type) [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [DiscreteTopology B] [Finite B] (T : Scheme.{u})
    (M N : FiniteDiscreteInternalModules B T) (f : M ⟶ N)
    (hM : IsConstructibleModuleObject
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj B) T) M)
    (hN : IsConstructibleModuleObject
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj B) T) N) :
    IsConstructibleModuleObject
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj B) T) (kernel f)
